title: A Well for the Bell
premise: When a construction crew in the dying town of Harrow's Bend unearths an iron door sealed from the inside, hospice nurse Ada Lockridge discovers her patients' backwards counting is a countdown to something beneath the town. The door belongs to the Bell, a well-shrine where, in 1974, six townspeople drowned a seventh — the bell-ringer Elias Vane — and stole his name to extend their own lives. Ada learns she is Elias's granddaughter, conceived to be the returned payment, and that the frost creeping through the town is the debt collecting itself. To end it, she must descend through the door, return what was taken — not Elias's life, but his name, which the surviving thieves still wear — choosing justice outside any law: she gives the name back at the cost of her own identity, dissolving into the well as the frost lifts and the town wakes remembering everything.
about_author: Tamsin Okafor is a former palliative care volunteer from coastal Maine who writes horror about the bargains small towns make with themselves. Her work has appeared in several underground anthologies; A Well for the Bell is her first novel.

chapters.title: The Counting Ward
chapters.summary: Ada Lockridge, night nurse at Harrow's Bend Hospice, hears her newest patient count down from ninety-one in his sleep, each number colder than the last. She documents it clinically, refusing superstition. POV: Ada. Beat: quiet dread established; her rationalism drawn as armor, already cracking.

chapters.title: What the Excavator Found
chapters.summary: Crews breaking ground for the new clinic annex strike iron twelve feet down: a door, bolted and welded from the inside, ringed by frost in July. Ada is called when a worker collapses, shivering. POV: Ada. Beat: intrusion of the impossible into the ordinary; the town's elders go strangely silent.

chapters.title: Ninety-One Reasons
chapters.summary: Ada cross-references patient records and finds every dying resident of Harrow's Bend counts backward, all converging on zero on the same date — the autumn equinox. Her supervisor, Marge Corliss, burns the printout. POV: Ada. Beat: institutional denial; first hint the living are complicit.

chapters.title: The Door That Opens Inward
chapters.summary: Ada dreams of standing before the door hearing a bell toll underwater. She wakes with frost on her window spelling a word: RETURN. At the site, the door now stands ajar though no one touched it. POV: Ada. Beat: the supernatural stops being deniable; invitation issued.

chapters.title: Six Names on a Plaque
chapters.summary: In the library's sealed local-history room, Ada finds a 1974 commemorative plaque honoring six founders — including Marge Corliss, impossibly young then. A seventh figure has been chiseled away. POV: Ada. Beat: mystery becomes history; the shape of a crime emerges.

chapters.title: Elias
chapters.summary: Ada's estranged mother, drunk and terrified, finally speaks: Ada's grandfather was Elias Vane, the bell-ringer who vanished in '74, and Ada was born 'to settle accounts.' She begs Ada to leave town. POV: Ada with mother interlude. Beat: personal stakes detonate; identity theme ignited.

chapters.title: Frostline
chapters.summary: The frost spreads along property lines exactly matching old survey maps, killing crops and pets in a pattern shaped like a bell. Townspeople begin forgetting small things — their middle names first. POV: Ada. Beat: escalating wrongness; the town itself is implicated.

chapters.title: The Survivors' Supper
chapters.summary: Marge invites Ada to dinner with the five other plaque names, all unnervingly preserved. They offer her money, then threats, then a story: Elias volunteered, they say. Their hands shake pouring tea. POV: Ada. Beat: power's corruption personified; wolves in cardigans.

chapters.title: Down the Well Shaft
chapters.summary: Ignoring every warning, Ada enters the door and finds not a room but a vertical shaft descending past strata of frozen years — 1974 visible like amber. Something below rings the bell once. POV: Ada. Beat: threshold crossed; wonder braided with terror.

chapters.title: Voices in the Ice
chapters.summary: In the shaft, Ada hears the drowned dead counting upward toward her, and among them a voice teaching her: the thieves took Elias's name, and a name held stolen keeps its owner alive and unfree. POV: Ada. Beat: rules of the haunting clarified; hope and horror entwined.

chapters.title: Marge's Confession, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Marge, unraveling as the frost takes her memories, half-confesses the drowning — 'we only wanted more time' — before her son silences her with a syringe. Ada realizes the families will kill to keep the name. POV: Ada. Beat: antagonist revealed as system, not villain; danger turns mortal.

chapters.title: The Clinic Annex
chapters.summary: The new clinic — built over the door — opens early, and its first patients begin counting. Ada understands the town's elite mean to feed the debt fresh souls rather than return anything. POV: Ada. Beat: moral stakes sharpened; justice must come from outside every institution.

chapters.title: Grandfather's Coat
chapters.summary: Searching her mother's attic, Ada finds Elias's bell-ringer coat and a ledger in his hand listing the six names beside six debts. Wearing the coat, she hears his voice clearly for the first time: not angry. Waiting. POV: Ada. Beat: inheritance accepted; grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Zero Hour Approaches
chapters.summary: With nine days left, the frost reaches Main Street. Patients hit single digits. The six families fortify the site with hired men and floodlights. Ada recruits the hospice's dying patients — the only ones who can hear the counting — as her witnesses. POV: Ada. Beat: alliance of the discarded; rising tension.

chapters.title: The Night the Bells Rang Themselves
chapters.summary: Every church bell in the county tolls at 3 a.m.; the hired guards flee. Ada breaks into the site and finds the shaft open, breathing cold, calling her by a name she never knew was hers: Vane. POV: Ada. Beat: point of no return; the debt knows her.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: The families capture Ada, intending to lower her into the well as substitute payment, arguing scripture and statute alike to justify it. Bound in the bell tower, she listens to them rehearse innocence. POV: Ada captive. Beat: darkest hour; power's corruption laid fully bare.

chapters.title: What the Dying Know
chapters.summary: Her patients, counting in unison across town, stall at one — holding the door shut long enough for Ada's ally, orderly Dev Osei, to cut her free. The dead below hold the line too. POV: Ada/Dev alternating. Beat: solidarity of the powerless; rescue earned, not given.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Ada goes down willingly, past frozen tableaux of 1974 — the six raising Elias over the well, his hands unbloodied, still ringing the bell as he fell. She reaches him and offers back the only thing she can: witness. POV: Ada. Beat: climax begins; compassion as weapon.

chapters.title: The Returning
chapters.summary: At the well's mouth, Ada speaks Elias's true name aloud, and it tears out of the six survivors across town like a pulled tooth — they collapse into their real ages as the frost reverses. But a name returned demands a vessel, and the well turns to her. POV: Ada. Beat: climax peak; justice exacted at terrible price.

chapters.title: Vane
chapters.summary: Choosing to give herself rather than let the well take another, Ada steps in — and finds Elias refuses the trade, taking her place in the dark while pushing her name back into her mouth. The bell rings once, whole. POV: Ada/Elias. Beat: sacrifice answered by grace; identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: Equinox Morning
chapters.summary: The frost melts overnight. The six survivors age and die within the week, remembered now as killers; the town wakes weeping with returned memory. The door seals itself, this time from the outside. Ada tends her last patients, who die in silence, at peace. POV: Ada. Beat: resolution; grief and release.

chapters.title: A Well for the Bell
chapters.summary: Months later, Ada stays in Harrow's Bend as its nurse, planting a garden over the filled shaft. Some nights she hears a single bell note under the soil — not a summons, a thank-you. She has learned that names are debts we owe each other, paid daily. POV: Ada. Beat: coda; quiet, changed, watchful peace.
